problem.title: Design a Linearizable Metadata & Config Store with Raft Lease Reads & Watchers
problem.tagline: Serving 100K RPS linearizable reads, CAS locks with fencing tokens, and 50K concurrent gRPC Watchers on a 5-node Raft cluster.
problem.purpose: Design an etcd/Chubby-grade metadata control plane that handles high-fanout service discovery reads, strictly ordered config watches, and split-brain-proof distributed leases.
problem.prompt: Design a linearizable metadata and configuration store (etcd/ZooKeeper scale) for a 10,000-node microservice fleet: 100K RPS linearizable reads, 5K RPS CAS writes, 50K concurrent Watch streams with zero missed revisions, and lease-backed leader locks.

prerequisites.title: Raft ReadIndex & Lease Reads
prerequisites.summary: Know how Batched ReadIndex and Monotonic Lease Reads serve linearizable reads without WAL writes.

prerequisites.title: MVCC Revisions & Fencing Tokens
prerequisites.summary: Understand monotonic global revision numbers for Watchers and why distributed locks need monotonic fencing tokens.

spark.summary: Pair a 5-node Raft cluster with MVCC B+Tree storage (global monotonic `revision`), Batched ReadIndex / Follower offload for 100K RPS reads, and multiplexed gRPC Watch streams.
spark.keyTakeaway: When building a linearizable control-plane metadata store, back every key with a global MVCC revision in Raft, serve reads via Batched ReadIndex + Follower offload, and multiplex Watchers over a single gRPC stream per node.
spark.byteSummary:
Control planes like Kubernetes (`etcd`) face an asymmetric workload: 5K writes/sec, 100K linearizable reads/sec, and 50,000 Watchers listening for config or endpoint changes. Putting all 50,000 Watchers on separate Raft proposals or polling loops crushes the cluster.

The architecture uses a 5-node Raft consensus group backed by an MVCC B+Tree (BoltDB-style) keyed by a monotonically increasing 64-bit `revision`. Every CAS write increments `revision` atomically upon Raft commit, enabling: (1) Lock-free Watchers that subscribe from `start_revision` and replay missed history from the MVCC log before switching to live pushes over multiplexed gRPC HTTP/2 streams; (2) Lease-backed distributed locks that return `revision` as a monotonic fencing token.

For 100K RPS linearizable reads, the Leader uses Batched ReadIndex (plus Follower ReadIndex offload) to serve reads from the in-memory B+Tree cache in <2 ms without touching the Raft WAL—while Watch Event Multiplexers coalesce thousands of Watchers onto ~10K gRPC connections.

learningJourney.title: R & E · Requirements, Revision Math & Watch Fanout Sizing
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Quantifies Raft WAL bandwidth, MVCC compaction windows, and Watch fanout traffic.

explanation.foundation: 5K CAS writes/sec x 2 KB = 10 MB/s of Raft log replication across 5 nodes—easily handled by NVMe WALs (<5 ms quorum `fsync`).
explanation.core: Illustrative Sizing: 100K reads/sec x 4 KB = 400 MB/s (3.2 Gbps) egress. A single Leader's 10 Gbps NIC can serve it, or offloading 80% to the 4 Followers via Follower ReadIndex drops per-node egress to 80 MB/s! For 50,000 Watchers receiving 100 config updates/sec, multiplexing 100 Watchers per gRPC HTTP/2 connection cuts TCP sockets from 50,000 to 500.
explanation.deepDive: Keep the total dataset bounded (e.g., <=8–16 GB of active metadata, compacted every 5 minutes by `revision`) so the entire MVCC B+Tree stays hot in OS/mmap RAM.

learningJourney.title: S · Storage: MVCC B+Tree Keyed by Monotonic Revision
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Shows how `(revision, sub_revision)` keys power both time-travel Watchers and fencing tokens.

explanation.foundation: Instead of overwriting keys in place, every Raft-committed `PUT` or `DELETE` writes a new MVCC tuple keyed by `(main_rev, sub_rev)`.
explanation.core: An in-memory `TreeIndex` maps `user_key -> [rev_1, rev_2, ...]` while BoltDB/B+Tree stores `rev -> {key, value, create_rev, mod_rev, version, lease_id}`. Watchers that disconnect at `rev = 10,400` reconnect with `watch(start_rev=10,401)` and catch up seamlessly from the B+Tree.
explanation.deepDive: Background MVCC Compaction periodically prunes revisions older than `latest_rev - retention_window` (e.g., 5 minutes), returning `CompactedError` if a Watcher was offline longer than retention so it knows to do a full `List` + `Watch` resync.

sectionDiagram.title: In-Memory TreeIndex (Key -> Revs) + BoltDB B+Tree (Rev -> Value)

learningJourney.title: H & A · 5-Node Raft + Follower ReadIndex + Watch Multiplexer
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Traces CAS writes, linearizable reads, and Watch event delivery end-to-end.

explanation.foundation: All writes (`PUT`, `CAS`, `LeaseGrant`) route to the Raft Leader, replicate to a 3/5 majority, and commit.
explanation.core: On commit, the state machine updates `TreeIndex` + BoltDB and immediately pushes `{key, rev, value}` into the local **Watch Event Multiplexer**, which fans out to all matching Watchers. Reads hit either Leader Lease/Batched ReadIndex or Follower ReadIndex (`Follower -> Leader.ReadIndex() -> local apply >= readIndex`).
explanation.deepDive: Multi-Region Note: Place 3 voting nodes in the primary region (or 2+2+1 across 3 AZs/regions with <10 ms RTT) and non-voting **Learner** nodes in distant regions for local `serializable` or `ReadIndex` reads without slowing down write quorum.

sectionDiagram.title: Writer CAS -> Raft Quorum Commit -> MVCC Apply -> Watch Push

learningJourney.title: D · Detailed Design: Leases, Fencing Tokens & Watch Catch-Up
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Prevents split-brain lock holders and slow-Watcher memory exhaustion.

explanation.foundation: Clients acquire distributed locks by attaching a TTL **Lease** (`LeaseGrant(ttl=10s)`) to a lock key via `CAS(create_rev == 0)`.
explanation.core: The store returns the lock key's `mod_revision` (e.g., `104`) as a **Fencing Token**. Downstream storage servers reject any write carrying `token < max_seen_token`, blocking a paused zombie lock holder even if its lease expired! If the client fails to send `LeaseKeepAlive` within 10s, the Leader proposes `LeaseRevoke` through Raft, deleting all attached keys and notifying Watchers.
explanation.deepDive: Slow Watcher Protection: If a Watch client stalls and stops reading its gRPC stream, never buffer unbounded events in RAM! Cap per-Watcher send buffers (e.g., 1,000 events) and demote stalled Watchers to `unsynced`—when they drain, they catch up directly from the BoltDB MVCC B+Tree.

codeExample.title: CAS Lock with Fencing Token & Bounded Watch Catch-Up
codeExample.code:
def acquire_fenced_lock(kv_store, lock_key, owner_id, lease_id):
    # Atomic Raft CAS: succeed only if key does not exist (create_rev == 0)
    ok, commit_rev = kv_store.txn_cas(
        if_create_rev=0,
        key=lock_key,
        value=owner_id,
        lease_id=lease_id,
    )
    if not ok:
        raise LockContentionError('Lock already held')
    return commit_rev  # Monotonic fencing token for downstream storage

decisionFramework.problem: How to scale Watchers and linearizable reads on a Raft metadata store without OOMing or stalling writes.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Buffer all Watch events per client in unbounded RAM and run all reads through the Raft WAL.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Slow Watch clients OOM the server; WAL reads cap cluster read QPS at disk `fsync` throughput.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Unbounded per-Watcher RAM queues vs. MVCC B+Tree Catch-Up + Bounded Buffers + ReadIndex.
decisionFramework.decision: Back Watchers with an MVCC B+Tree (`unsynced` fallback on slow consumers), multiplex over HTTP/2, and serve reads via Batched ReadIndex + Follower offload.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Requires periodic MVCC compaction (forcing very stale Watchers to `List` + `Watch`) in exchange for bounded RAM and 100K RPS reads.

decisionExercise.prompt: A Watch client pauses for 20 minutes while MVCC compaction runs every 5 minutes. When it reconnects with `start_revision = 5,000` (already compacted), what must the metadata store return?

options.label: Return `CompactedError` (with `compact_revision`) so the client performs a fresh linearizable `List` snapshot and restarts `Watch` from that snapshot's revision.
options.explanation: Correct! Silently skipping compacted revisions would cause missed deletes/updates; `CompactedError` triggers a safe List+Watch resync.

options.label: Start streaming from the latest revision and ignore the gap.
options.explanation: Skipping events breaks state synchronization for controllers like Kubernetes.

options.label: Disable MVCC compaction permanently.
options.explanation: Disabling compaction causes unbounded disk and RAM growth.

sectionDiagram.title: Synced (Live Mux) -> Slow Buffer Full (Unsynced) -> MVCC Catch-Up -> Compacted

learningJourney.title: E & D · Evaluation, Assumptions, Limitations & Glossary
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Documents dataset size caps, Raft quorum limits, and control-plane terminology.

explanation.foundation: Raft metadata stores are designed for small, critical control-plane state (<=8–16 GB), not bulk blob or event storage.
explanation.core: Assumptions & Limitations: Sizing assumes <=16 GB live MVCC state, <=10 ms intra-region RTT across 5 voting nodes, and periodic 5-minute MVCC compaction. Storing multi-GB payloads or millions of keys per second in Raft saturates BoltDB write transactions and heartbeat timers, risking spurious leader elections.
explanation.deepDive: Glossary: MVCC Revision (global monotonic 64-bit counter incremented per Raft transaction); CAS (Compare-And-Swap on `mod_revision` or `create_revision`); Fencing Token (monotonic token blocking stale lock holders); Learner Node (non-voting Raft replica scaling read-only locality).

knowledgeChecks.question: How does an etcd-style metadata store let a disconnected Watch client resume without missing any config updates?

options.text: Every write is stored under a global monotonic `revision` in an MVCC B+Tree, so Watchers reconnect with `start_revision = last_seen + 1`.
options.feedback: Correct! MVCC revision history lets Watchers replay missed events until caught up to live head.

options.text: The server keeps an infinite per-client RAM queue forever.
options.feedback: Unbounded per-client RAM queues would OOM the server on slow clients.

options.text: Clients broadcast UDP packets to all 5 Raft nodes.
options.feedback: Watchers use multiplexed gRPC HTTP/2 streams.
Compaction runs periodically; very old Watchers receive `CompactedError` and resync via List+Watch.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Global MVCC revisions decouple Watch durability from bounded per-connection RAM buffers.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a distributed lock backed by a Raft Lease also return `mod_revision` as a Fencing Token?

options.text: So downstream storage can reject late writes from a paused zombie lock holder whose lease expired while it was stalled.
options.feedback: Correct! Downstream servers enforce `token >= max_seen_token`, preventing split-brain overwrites.

options.text: To encrypt the gRPC Watch stream.
options.feedback: TLS encrypts gRPC; fencing tokens order resource writes.

options.text: To skip Raft majority quorum on writes.
options.feedback: Lock acquisition still requires Raft quorum.

options.text: To double the LeaseKeepAlive TTL automatically.
options.feedback: Fencing tokens do not modify lease TTLs.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Leases alone cannot stop a paused client from sending an already-in-flight write; monotonic fencing tokens close that race.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a Raft metadata store enforce a strict dataset size limit (e.g., 8–16 GB) and regular MVCC compaction?

options.text: To keep the MVCC B+Tree hot in memory and prevent large snapshots/compactions from stalling Raft heartbeat timers.
options.feedback: Correct! Bloated MVCC tables cause slow BoltDB commits and Raft snapshot stalls that trigger spurious elections.

options.text: Because gRPC cannot send payloads larger than 8 GB total per year.
options.feedback: The limit is about state-machine memory and snapshot stability, not gRPC.
Keeping state compact makes Follower ReadIndex faster.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Metadata stores are optimized for compact, high-consistency control-plane state, not bulk storage.

beginner.summary: Build a strongly consistent config and lock store using a 5-node Raft cluster, versioned MVCC keys, and multiplexed Watch streams.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When building a reliable config and lock service, store every change with a version number in Raft so Watchers never miss updates and locks stay safe.
beginner.byteSummary: A 5-node Raft cluster stores every config update with a monotonic revision number, serves fast reads via ReadIndex, and pushes live updates to 50K Watchers over shared HTTP/2 streams.

intermediate.summary: Combine 5-node Raft + MVCC BoltDB (`revision`), Batched ReadIndex + Follower offload for 100K RPS reads, and bounded-buffer gRPC Watch multiplexing.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: When designing an etcd-scale metadata store, back Watchers with MVCC revision catch-up, protect locks with fencing tokens, and offload reads via ReadIndex.
intermediate.byteSummary: MVCC revisions enable seamless Watch catch-up and monotonic fencing tokens, while Batched ReadIndex + Follower offload serves 100K RPS reads without touching the WAL.

advanced.summary: 5-node Raft + MVCC BoltDB/TreeIndex, 5-minute revision compaction with `CompactedError` resync, `unsynced` slow-Watcher demotion, and Learner-node read scaling.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When operating a 100K-RPS control plane, bound per-Watcher RAM via `unsynced` MVCC fallback, enforce 8–16 GB state caps, and offload reads with ReadIndex.
advanced.byteSummary: Pairing `unsynced` MVCC B+Tree catch-up, 5-minute revision compaction, `mod_revision` fencing tokens, and Batched/Follower ReadIndex keeps p99 <2 ms with zero missed Watch events.
